    optimize_prior_precision(
    pred_type: PredType | str = PredType.GLM,
    method: TuningMethod | str = TuningMethod.MARGLIK,
    n_steps: int = 100,
    lr: float = 0.1,
    init_prior_prec: float | Tensor = 1.0,
    prior_structure: (
        PriorStructure | str
    ) = PriorStructure.SCALAR,
    val_loader: DataLoader | None = None,
    loss: (
        Metric | Callable[[Tensor], Tensor | float] | None
    ) = None,
    log_prior_prec_min: float = -4,
    log_prior_prec_max: float = 4,
    grid_size: int = 100,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str = LinkApprox.PROBIT,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    verbose: bool = False,
    progress_bar: bool = False,
    log_prior_prec_base: float = 10.0,
) -> None

    Optimize the prior precision post-hoc using the method specified by the user.

    Parameters:

    • pred_type (PredType or str in {'glm', 'nn'}) –

      type of posterior predictive, linearized GLM predictive or neural network sampling predictiv. The GLM predictive is consistent with the curvature approximations used here.

    • method (TuningMethod or str in {'marglik', 'gridsearch'}, default: PredType.MARGLIK ) –

      specifies how the prior precision should be optimized.

    • n_steps (int, default: 100 ) –

      the number of gradient descent steps to take.

    • lr (float, default: 1e-1 ) –

      the learning rate to use for gradient descent.

    • init_prior_prec (float or tensor, default: 1.0 ) –

      initial prior precision before the first optimization step.

    • prior_structure (PriorStructure or str in {'scalar', 'layerwise', 'diag'}, default: PriorStructure.SCALAR ) –

      if init_prior_prec is scalar, the prior precision is optimized with this structure. otherwise, the structure of init_prior_prec is maintained.

    • val_loader (DataLoader, default: None ) –

      DataLoader for the validation set; each iterate is a training batch (X, y).

    • loss (callable or Metric, default: None ) –

      loss function to use for CV. If callable, the loss is computed offline (memory intensive). If torchmetrics.Metric, running loss is computed (efficient). The default depends on the likelihood: RunningNLLMetric() for classification and reward modeling, with the ignore_index of a CategoricalLikelihood, RunningBernoulliNLLMetric() for the Bernoulli likelihood, RunningGaussianNLLMetric() for the heteroscedastic Gaussian likelihood, and for regression RunningGaussianNLLMetric with the noise variance of the likelihood. Other likelihoods have no default, so loss is required for them.

    • log_prior_prec_min (float, default: -4 ) –

      exponent of the lower bound of the gridsearch interval.

    • log_prior_prec_max (float, default: 4 ) –

      exponent of the upper bound of the gridsearch interval.

    • grid_size (int, default: 100 ) –

      number of values to consider inside the gridsearch interval.

    • link_approx (LinkApprox or str in {'mc', 'probit', 'bridge'}, default: LinkApprox.PROBIT ) –

      how to approximate the classification link function for the 'glm'. For pred_type='nn', only 'mc' is possible.

    • n_samples (int, default: 100 ) –

      number of samples for link_approx='mc'.

    • verbose (bool, default: False ) –

      if true, the optimized prior precision will be printed (can be a large tensor if the prior has a diagonal covariance).

    • progress_bar (bool, default: False ) –

      whether to show a progress bar; updated at every batch-Hessian computation. Useful for very large model and large amount of data, esp. when subset_of_weights='all'.

    • log_prior_prec_base (float, default: 10.0 ) –

      base of the logarithmic gridsearch interval. The bounds are log_prior_prec_base raised to log_prior_prec_min and log_prior_prec_max.

    self,
    pred_type: PredType | str = PredType.GLM,
    method: TuningMethod | str = TuningMethod.MARGLIK,
    n_steps: int = 100,
    lr: float = 1e-1,
    init_prior_prec: float | torch.Tensor = 1.0,
    prior_structure: PriorStructure | str = PriorStructure.SCALAR,
    val_loader: DataLoader | None = None,

        link_approx,

        verbose,
        progress_bar,
        log_prior_prec_base=log_prior_prec_base,

    def _glm_predictive_marginals(
    self, x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Mean and variance of each output of the GLM predictive, without the
    covariances between outputs. Override it when the variances are cheaper to
    get than the full output covariance.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        inputs, as in `__call__`.

    Returns
    -------
    f_mu : torch.Tensor
        predictive mean `(batch, outputs)`
    f_var : torch.Tensor
        predictive variances `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    f_mu, f_var = self._glm_predictive_distribution(x)

    return f_mu, torch.diagonal(f_var, dim1=-2, dim2=-1)

    Parameters:

    • x (Tensor or MutableMapping) –

      (batch_size, input_shape) if tensor. If MutableMapping, must contain the said tensor.

    • likelihood (Likelihood or str) –

      likelihood of the predictive. A Gaussian one returns the predictive moments. Classification and reward modeling return class probabilities from link_approx. Any other likelihood returns the Monte Carlo estimate of \(\mathbb{E}[g(f)]\) under the GLM predictive \(f \sim \mathcal{N}(f_\mu, \Sigma_f)\), where \(g\) is its inverse_link, from n_samples draws.

    • link_approx (('mc', 'probit', 'bridge', 'bridge_norm'), default: 'mc' ) –

      how to approximate the classification link function for the 'glm'. For pred_type='nn', only 'mc' is possible. Likelihoods other than classification, reward modeling and Bernoulli always use Monte Carlo.

    • joint (bool, default: False ) –

      Whether to output a joint predictive distribution in regression with pred_type='glm'. If set to True, the predictive distribution has the same form as GP posterior, i.e. N([f(x1), ...,f(xm)], Cov[f(x1), ..., f(xm)]). If False, then only outputs the marginal predictive distribution. Only available for regression and GLM predictive.

    • n_samples (int, default: 100 ) –

      number of samples for link_approx='mc' and for the Monte Carlo predictive of other likelihoods.

    • diagonal_output (bool, default: False ) –

      whether to use a diagonalized posterior predictive on the outputs. Only works for pred_type='glm' and link_approx='mc', or for the Monte Carlo predictive of other likelihoods.

    • generator (Generator, default: None ) –

      random number generator for the Monte Carlo samples.

    Returns:

    • predictive ( Tensor or tuple[Tensor] ) –

      For likelihood='classification', a torch.Tensor is returned with a distribution over classes (similar to a Softmax), with the same shape as the logits, e.g. (batch, classes) or (batch, seq_len, classes). For likelihood='regression', a tuple of torch.Tensor is returned with the mean and the predictive variance. For likelihood='regression' and joint=True, a tuple of torch.Tensor is returned with the mean and the predictive covariance. For any other likelihood, a torch.Tensor is returned with the predictive mean of the targets, with the shape of the outputs, e.g. (batch, outputs).

    Warns:

    • RuntimeWarning –

      For "bridge" and "bridge_norm" when gradient tracking is enabled and a covariance requiring gradients has subnormal, nonzero magnitude for an input row. Magnitude is the largest absolute covariance entry, compared with the smallest positive normal value of the covariance dtype.

    Notes

    The "bridge" and "bridge_norm" links use float64 intermediate calculations and return probabilities in the predictive mean's dtype. Mean corrections and normalization use scaled logit differences to avoid overflow. If corrected variances or the optional normalization scale are nonpositive, or the Bridge probabilities are nonfinite, prediction uses the probit approximation on centered moments before variance normalization. Corrected variances are clamped at zero for this fallback.

    For subnormal covariance magnitudes, covariance-entry derivatives can exceed their dtype's range. Covariance or upstream parameter gradients may therefore contain inf or NaN even when probabilities remain finite. Covariance backpropagation is not reliable in this regime. A RuntimeWarning is emitted when covariance gradients are tracked.

    def _glm_forward_call(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping,
    likelihood: Likelihood | str,
    joint: bool = False,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str = LinkApprox.PROBIT,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    diagonal_output: bool = False,
    generator: torch.Generator | None = None,
) -> torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute the posterior predictive on input data `x` for "glm" pred type.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        `(batch_size, input_shape)` if tensor. If MutableMapping, must contain
        the said tensor.

    likelihood : Likelihood or str
        likelihood of the predictive. A Gaussian one returns the predictive
        moments. Classification and reward modeling return class probabilities
        from `link_approx`. Any other likelihood returns the Monte Carlo
        estimate of \\(\\mathbb{E}[g(f)]\\) under the GLM predictive
        \\(f \\sim \\mathcal{N}(f_\\mu, \\Sigma_f)\\), where \\(g\\) is its
        `inverse_link`, from `n_samples` draws.

    link_approx : {'mc', 'probit', 'bridge', 'bridge_norm'}
        how to approximate the classification link function for the `'glm'`.
        For `pred_type='nn'`, only 'mc' is possible. Likelihoods other than
        classification, reward modeling and Bernoulli always use Monte Carlo.

    joint : bool
        Whether to output a joint predictive distribution in regression with
        `pred_type='glm'`. If set to `True`, the predictive distribution
        has the same form as GP posterior, i.e. N([f(x1), ...,f(xm)], Cov[f(x1), ..., f(xm)]).
        If `False`, then only outputs the marginal predictive distribution.
        Only available for regression and GLM predictive.

    n_samples : int
        number of samples for `link_approx='mc'` and for the Monte Carlo
        predictive of other likelihoods.

    diagonal_output : bool
        whether to use a diagonalized posterior predictive on the outputs.
        Only works for `pred_type='glm'` and `link_approx='mc'`, or for the
        Monte Carlo predictive of other likelihoods.

    generator : torch.Generator, optional
        random number generator for the Monte Carlo samples.

    Returns
    -------
    predictive: torch.Tensor or tuple[torch.Tensor]
        For `likelihood='classification'`, a torch.Tensor is returned with
        a distribution over classes (similar to a Softmax), with the same shape
        as the logits, e.g. `(batch, classes)` or `(batch, seq_len, classes)`.
        For `likelihood='regression'`, a tuple of torch.Tensor is returned
        with the mean and the predictive variance.
        For `likelihood='regression'` and `joint=True`, a tuple of torch.Tensor
        is returned with the mean and the predictive covariance.
        For any other likelihood, a torch.Tensor is returned with the predictive
        mean of the targets, with the shape of the outputs, e.g.
        `(batch, outputs)`.

    Warns
    -----
    RuntimeWarning
        For ``"bridge"`` and ``"bridge_norm"`` when gradient tracking is
        enabled and a covariance requiring gradients has subnormal,
        nonzero magnitude for an input row. Magnitude is the largest
        absolute covariance entry, compared with the smallest positive
        normal value of the covariance dtype.

    Notes
    -----
    The ``"bridge"`` and ``"bridge_norm"`` links use float64 intermediate
    calculations and return probabilities in the predictive mean's dtype.
    Mean corrections and normalization use scaled logit differences to
    avoid overflow.
    If corrected variances or the optional normalization scale are
    nonpositive, or the Bridge probabilities are nonfinite, prediction uses
    the probit approximation on centered moments before variance
    normalization. Corrected variances are clamped at zero for this fallback.

    For subnormal covariance magnitudes, covariance-entry derivatives can
    exceed their dtype's range. Covariance or upstream parameter gradients
    may therefore contain inf or NaN even when probabilities remain finite.
    Covariance backpropagation is not reliable in this regime. A
    RuntimeWarning is emitted when covariance gradients are tracked.
    """
    likelihood = get_likelihood(likelihood)
    is_gaussian = likelihood.is_gaussian

    if is_gaussian and diagonal_output and not joint:
        return self._glm_predictive_marginals(x)

    f_mu, f_var = self._glm_predictive_distribution(x, joint=joint and is_gaussian)

    if is_gaussian:
        return f_mu, f_var

    if likelihood.name == Likelihood.BERNOULLI.name:
        # Every output has its own sigmoid, so the probit approximation needs only
        # the marginal variances. MC falls through to the generic path below.
        if link_approx == LinkApprox.PROBIT:
            kappa = 1 / torch.sqrt(
                1.0 + np.pi / 8 * torch.diagonal(f_var, dim1=-2, dim2=-1)
            )
            return likelihood.inverse_link(kappa * f_mu)

        if link_approx != LinkApprox.MC:
            raise ValueError(
                "The Laplace bridge is for the softmax link only. Use 'probit' or "
                "'mc' with the Bernoulli likelihood."
            )

    if likelihood.name not in _CATEGORICAL_NAMES:
        # No closed form to approximate, so integrate the inverse link by MC
        f_samples = self._glm_functional_samples(
            f_mu, f_var, n_samples, diagonal_output, generator
        )
        return likelihood.inverse_link(f_samples).mean(dim=0)

    # Every leading dim of the logits but the last is a batch dim, e.g. `(B, L, C)`
    # for sequences. The link approximations work on `(N, C)`, so flatten them.
    batch_shape = f_mu.shape[:-1]
    f_mu = f_mu.reshape(-1, f_mu.shape[-1])
    f_var = f_var.reshape(-1, *f_var.shape[-2:])

    probs = self._glm_classification_link(
        f_mu, f_var, likelihood, link_approx, n_samples, diagonal_output, generator
    )
    return probs.reshape(*batch_shape, probs.shape[-1])

    def _glm_classification_link(
    self,
    f_mu: torch.Tensor,
    f_var: torch.Tensor,
    likelihood: Likelihood,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str,
    n_samples: int,
    diagonal_output: bool,
    generator: torch.Generator | None = None,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Approximate the predictive class probabilities from the GLM predictive
    `f_mu` `(batch, classes)` and `f_var` `(batch, classes, classes)`. `likelihood`
    is the staged likelihood, categorical while fitting a reward model. See
    `_glm_forward_call` for the other arguments.
    """
    if link_approx == LinkApprox.MC:
        f_samples = self._glm_functional_samples(
            f_mu, f_var, n_samples, diagonal_output, generator
        )
        return likelihood.inverse_link(f_samples).mean(dim=0)
    elif link_approx == LinkApprox.PROBIT:
        kappa = 1 / torch.sqrt(1.0 + np.pi / 8 * f_var.diagonal(dim1=1, dim2=2))
        return torch.softmax(kappa * f_mu, dim=-1)
    elif "bridge" in link_approx:
        _, K = f_mu.shape
        if K == 1:
            return torch.ones_like(f_mu)

        # Float32 reductions can overflow even when every input is finite.
        # Keep the link calculation in double precision, then restore the
        # predictive dtype at the return boundary.
        output_dtype, covariance_dtype = f_mu.dtype, f_var.dtype
        work_dtype = torch.promote_types(output_dtype, covariance_dtype)
        if work_dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32):
            work_dtype = torch.float64
        f_mu, f_var = f_mu.to(work_dtype), f_var.to(work_dtype)

        # Normalize covariance before reductions: even float64 sums can
        # overflow when each covariance entry is finite. The scale
        # cancels in the ratio, so detach it to avoid unstable gradients
        # through the normalization itself.
        covariance_scale = f_var.detach().abs().amax(dim=(1, 2), keepdim=True)
        if (
            torch.is_grad_enabled()
            and f_var.requires_grad
            and (
                (covariance_scale > 0)
                & (covariance_scale < torch.finfo(covariance_dtype).tiny)
            ).any()
        ):
            warnings.warn(
                "Bridge covariance gradients may overflow for subnormal covariance, "
                "even when probabilities are finite. Covariance and upstream "
                "parameter gradients may contain inf or NaN; covariance "
                "backpropagation is not reliable at this scale.",
                RuntimeWarning,
                stacklevel=3,
            )
        safe_covariance_scale = torch.where(
            covariance_scale > 0, covariance_scale, 1
        )
        scaled_covariance = f_var / safe_covariance_scale
        row_sums = scaled_covariance.sum(dim=-1)
        sum_variance = row_sums.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True).unsqueeze(-1)
        centered = sum_variance.abs() <= (
            torch.finfo(covariance_dtype).eps
            * scaled_covariance.abs().sum(dim=(1, 2), keepdim=True)
        )
        safe_variance = torch.where(centered, 1, sum_variance)
        ratio = torch.where(
            centered.squeeze(-1), 0, row_sums / safe_variance.squeeze(-1)
        )

        # Keep the mean correction scaled: even subtracting two finite
        # float64 means can overflow. Only restore the scale after removing
        # a common shift, since Bridge depends on logit differences.
        mean_magnitude = f_mu.detach().abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        _, mean_exponent = torch.frexp(mean_magnitude)
        # Bound both scales to leave headroom for normalization gradients.
        # A power of two preserves representable logit differences; exp2
        # with an explicit dtype is independent of the global default.
        logit_limit = sqrt(sqrt(torch.finfo(work_dtype).max))
        max_mean_exponent = frexp(logit_limit)[1] - 1
        mean_scale = torch.exp2(
            (mean_exponent - 1).clamp(0, max_mean_exponent).to(work_dtype)
        )
        scaled_mean = f_mu / mean_scale
        mean_logit = (scaled_mean / K).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        scaled_mean = scaled_mean - torch.where(
            centered.squeeze(-1),
            mean_logit,
            (K * ratio) * mean_logit,
        )
        f_mu = scaled_mean - scaled_mean.amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        centered_covariance = scaled_covariance - ratio.unsqueeze(
            -1
        ) * row_sums.unsqueeze(-2)
        scaled_var_diag = centered_covariance.diagonal(dim1=-2, dim2=-1)
        centered_var_diag = scaled_var_diag * safe_covariance_scale.squeeze(-1)
        valid_variance = (centered_var_diag > 0).all(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        normalization = torch.ones_like(mean_scale)

        if link_approx == LinkApprox.BRIDGE_NORM:
            variance_scale = (centered_var_diag / K).sum(
                dim=-1, keepdim=True
            ) / sqrt(K / 2)
            valid_variance = valid_variance & (variance_scale > 0)
            normalization = torch.where(valid_variance, variance_scale, 1).sqrt()

        # Bound normalized differences before division, so saturated
        # branches cannot overflow in either forward or backward passes.
        # The detached bound is far beyond exponential underflow; large
        # variances still bring extreme gaps back into a meaningful range.
        minimum_logit = -(logit_limit / mean_scale) * normalization.detach()
        f_mu = (f_mu.clamp_min(minimum_logit) / normalization) * mean_scale

        # Normalize the Bridge's Dirichlet parameters in log space.
        # The log-sum-exp term is common to every class and cancels in
        # the final softmax. Remove it before combining the numerator
        # terms, avoiding overflow when finite logit gaps are enormous.
        log_sum_negative = torch.logsumexp(-f_mu, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        log_base = log(1 - 2 / K) if K > 2 else -float("inf")
        log_numerator = torch.logaddexp(
            torch.full_like(f_mu, log_base) - log_sum_negative,
            f_mu - 2 * log(K),
        )
        # Remove the common offset before subtracting log-variance,
        # preserving variance-dependent weights for tied large logits.
        log_numerator = log_numerator - log_numerator.amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        if K == 2:
            # Binary corrected variances are equal for symmetric covariance.
            # Cancel their common term before differentiation to avoid
            # overflowing gradients for subnormal covariance.
            log_alpha = log_numerator
        else:
            # Common covariance and optional variance scales cancel in alpha
            # normalization. Logging the scaled diagonal avoids reciprocals
            # of subnormal variances in backpropagation.
            log_alpha = (
                log_numerator
                - scaled_var_diag.clamp_min(torch.finfo(work_dtype).tiny).log()
            )
        probabilities = torch.softmax(log_alpha, dim=-1)

        # A common shift of every logit has no effect on softmax. The
        # fallback therefore uses the centered moments before Bridge's
        # optional variance normalization.
        fallback_logits = scaled_mean / torch.sqrt(
            1 + np.pi / 8 * centered_var_diag.clamp_min(0)
        )
        fallback_logits = fallback_logits - fallback_logits.amax(
            dim=-1, keepdim=True
        )
        fallback_logits = (
            fallback_logits.clamp_min(-logit_limit / mean_scale) * mean_scale
        )
        fallback = torch.softmax(fallback_logits, dim=-1)
        valid_variance = valid_variance & torch.isfinite(probabilities).all(
            dim=-1, keepdim=True
        )
        return torch.where(valid_variance, probabilities, fallback).to(output_dtype)
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            "Prediction path invalid. Check the likelihood, pred_type, link_approx combination!"
        )

    @joins_outputs
def functional_samples(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    pred_type: PredType | str = PredType.GLM,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    diagonal_output: bool = False,
    generator: torch.Generator | None = None,
    joint: bool = False,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Sample from the function-space posterior on input data `x`.
    Can be used, for example, to compute an arbitrary expectation, or with
    `joint=True` for Thompson sampling.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        input data `(batch_size, input_shape)`

    pred_type : {'glm', 'nn'}, default='glm'
        type of posterior predictive, linearized GLM predictive or neural
        network sampling predictive. The GLM predictive is consistent with
        the curvature approximations used here.

    n_samples : int
        number of samples

    diagonal_output : bool
        whether to use a diagonalized glm posterior predictive on the outputs.
        Only applies when `pred_type='glm'`.

    generator : torch.Generator, optional
        random number generator to control the samples (if sampling used)

    joint : bool, default=False
        whether to sample all inputs in `x` jointly. With `joint=False`, each
        input's marginal is correct but the samples ignore the correlation
        between inputs. Use `joint=True` for Thompson sampling or batch
        acquisition functions such as qEI. The joint covariance has
        `(batch_size * outputs)**2` entries, so memory grows quadratically
        with the batch. Extra batch dimensions are flattened into
        `batch_size`. Ignored when `pred_type='nn'`, since one weight sample
        already gives one function over all inputs.

    Returns
    -------
    samples : torch.Tensor
        samples `(n_samples, batch_size, output_shape)`
    """
    if pred_type not in PredType.__members__.values():
        raise ValueError("Only glm and nn supported as prediction types.")

    if pred_type == PredType.GLM and joint:
        f_mu, f_cov = self._glm_predictive_distribution(x, joint=True)

        # Reward models are fitted on pairs but predict one reward per item
        n_outputs = self._n_predictive_outputs

        if diagonal_output:
            # Keep the covariance between inputs, drop it between outputs
            output_ids = torch.arange(f_mu.numel(), device=f_mu.device)
            output_ids = output_ids % n_outputs
            f_cov = f_cov * (output_ids[:, None] == output_ids[None, :])

        samples = draw_gaussian(f_mu, f_cov, n_samples, generator)
        return samples.reshape(n_samples, -1, n_outputs)
    elif pred_type == PredType.GLM:
        f_mu, f_var = self._glm_predictive_distribution(x)
        return self._glm_functional_samples(
            f_mu, f_var, n_samples, diagonal_output, generator
        )
    else:  # 'nn'
        return self._nn_functional_samples(x, n_samples, generator)

    def _glm_functional_samples(
    self,
    f_mu: torch.Tensor,
    f_var: torch.Tensor,
    n_samples: int,
    diagonal_output: bool = False,
    generator: torch.Generator | None = None,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Sample from the posterior functional on input data `x` using "glm" prediction
    type.

    Parameters
    ----------
    f_mu : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        glm predictive mean `([batch_dims], output_shape)`

    f_var : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        glm predictive covariances `([batch_dims], output_shape, output_shape)`

    n_samples : int
        number of samples

    diagonal_output : bool
        whether to use a diagonalized glm posterior predictive on the outputs.

    generator : torch.Generator, optional
        random number generator to control the samples (if sampling used)

    Returns
    -------
    samples : torch.Tensor
        samples `(n_samples, [batch_dims], output_shape)`
    """
    # Flatten the batch dims (e.g. batch and sequence), sample, then restore them
    batch_shape = f_mu.shape[:-1]
    f_mu = f_mu.reshape(-1, f_mu.shape[-1])
    f_var = f_var.reshape(-1, *f_var.shape[-2:])
    assert f_var.shape == torch.Size([f_mu.shape[0], f_mu.shape[1], f_mu.shape[1]])

    if diagonal_output:
        f_var = torch.diagonal(f_var, dim1=-2, dim2=-1)

    samples = normal_samples(f_mu, f_var, n_samples, generator)
    return samples.reshape(n_samples, *batch_shape, f_mu.shape[-1])

    @staticmethod
def _check_classification_targets(out: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    """Check that the targets match the logits `out` `(batch, ..., classes)`:
    either class indices `(batch, ...)` or floating-point class probabilities
    `(batch, ..., classes)`.

    Only the number of dims and the class dim are checked, since `out` is
    computed on a single datum and the sequence length can vary between batches.
    The backends check the exact shapes against the logits of each batch.

    Parameters
    ----------
    out : torch.Tensor
        logits of a single datum, `(1, ..., classes)`.
    y : torch.Tensor
        targets of a batch.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        if the targets are neither class indices nor class probabilities, or if
        they have the shape of class probabilities but an integer dtype.
    """
    is_index = y.ndim == out.ndim - 1
    is_prob = y.ndim == out.ndim and y.shape[-1] == out.shape[-1]

    if not (is_index or is_prob):
        raise ValueError(
            f"The model's logits have {out.ndim} dims (batch, ..., classes), but "
            f"the targets have {y.ndim} dims. The targets must be class indices "
            f"with {out.ndim - 1} dims, or class probabilities with {out.ndim} "
            f"dims and {out.shape[-1]} classes in the last one."
        )

    if is_prob and not y.is_floating_point():
        raise ValueError(
            f"The targets have the shape of class probabilities, but their dtype "
            f"is {y.dtype}. Call `.float()` on one-hot targets, or pass class "
            f"indices without the class dim, i.e. with {out.ndim - 1} "
            f"{'dim' if out.ndim == 2 else 'dims'}."
        )

    def log_prob(self, value: torch.Tensor, normalized: bool = True) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Compute the log probability under the (current) Laplace approximation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    value: torch.Tensor
    normalized : bool, default=True
        whether to return log of a properly normalized Gaussian or just the
        terms that depend on `value`.

    Returns
    -------
    log_prob : torch.Tensor
    """
    if not normalized:
        return -self.square_norm(value) / 2
    log_prob = (
        -self.n_params / 2 * log(2 * pi) + self.log_det_posterior_precision / 2
    )
    log_prob -= self.square_norm(value) / 2
    return log_prob

    def _predictive(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    likelihood: Likelihood,
    pred_type: PredType | str,
    joint: bool,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str,
    n_samples: int,
    diagonal_output: bool,
    generator: torch.Generator | None,
    **model_kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """The posterior predictive of `__call__` for the staged `likelihood`, after
    the arguments are checked."""
    if pred_type == PredType.GLM:
        return self._glm_forward_call(
            x, likelihood, joint, link_approx, n_samples, diagonal_output, generator
        )
    else:
        if likelihood.is_gaussian:
            samples = self._nn_predictive_samples(
                x, n_samples, generator, **model_kwargs
            )
            return samples.mean(dim=0), samples.var(dim=0)
        elif likelihood.name in _CATEGORICAL_NAMES:
            # The average is computed online
            return self._nn_predictive_classification(
                x, n_samples, generator, **model_kwargs
            )
        else:
            f_samples = self._nn_functional_samples(
                x, n_samples, generator, **model_kwargs
            )
            return likelihood.inverse_link(f_samples).mean(dim=0)

    def _aleatoric_variance(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    joint: bool = False,
    **model_kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Variance that a heteroscedastic network predicts at the MAP.

    The model runs without the hook of `joined_outputs`, so the variance keeps
    its graph with `enable_backprop=True`, e.g. for gradients w.r.t. the inputs.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        inputs, as in `__call__`.
    joint : bool, default=False
        whether to flatten the variance, as the mean of the joint predictive.

    Returns
    -------
    f_alea : torch.Tensor
        `(batch, ..., K)`, or `(batch * ... * K,)` if `joint`.
    """
    x = x.to(self._device) if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) else x

    with torch.set_grad_enabled(self.enable_backprop and torch.is_grad_enabled()):
        out = as_joined_outputs(self.model(x, **model_kwargs))

    var = self.likelihood.split(out)[1]

    if not self.enable_backprop:
        var = var.detach()

    return var.flatten() if joint else var

    @joins_outputs
def predictive_samples(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    pred_type: PredType | str = PredType.GLM,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    diagonal_output: bool = False,
    generator: torch.Generator | None = None,
    joint: bool = False,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Sample from the posterior predictive on input data `x`. I.e., the respective
    inverse-link function (e.g. softmax) is applied on top of the functional
    sample.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        input data `(batch_size, input_shape)`

    pred_type : {'glm', 'nn'}, default='glm'
        type of posterior predictive, linearized GLM predictive or neural
        network sampling predictive. The GLM predictive is consistent with
        the curvature approximations used here.

    n_samples : int
        number of samples

    diagonal_output : bool
        whether to use a diagonalized glm posterior predictive on the outputs.
        Only applies when `pred_type='glm'`.

    generator : torch.Generator, optional
        random number generator to control the samples (if sampling used)

    joint : bool, default=False
        whether to sample all inputs in `x` jointly. With `joint=False`, each
        input's marginal is correct but the samples ignore the correlation
        between inputs. Use `joint=True` for Thompson sampling or batch
        acquisition functions such as qEI. The joint covariance has
        `(batch_size * outputs)**2` entries, so memory grows quadratically
        with the batch. Extra batch dimensions are flattened into
        `batch_size`. Ignored when `pred_type='nn'`, since one weight sample
        already gives one function over all inputs.

    Returns
    -------
    samples : torch.Tensor
        samples `(n_samples, batch_size, output_shape)`
    """
    if pred_type not in PredType.__members__.values():
        raise ValueError("Only glm and nn supported as prediction types.")

    if pred_type == PredType.GLM and joint:
        f_samples = self.functional_samples(
            x, pred_type, n_samples, diagonal_output, generator, joint=True
        )

        return self.likelihood.predictive_likelihood.inverse_link(f_samples)
    elif pred_type == PredType.GLM:
        f_mu, f_var = self._glm_predictive_distribution(x)
        return self._glm_predictive_samples(
            f_mu, f_var, n_samples, diagonal_output, generator
        )
    else:  # 'nn'
        return self._nn_predictive_samples(x, n_samples, generator)

    functional_variance(Js: Tensor) -> Tensor

    Compute functional variance for the 'glm' predictive: f_var[i] = Js[i] @ P.inv() @ Js[i].T, which is a output x output predictive covariance matrix. Mathematically, we have for a single Jacobian \(\mathcal{J} = \nabla_\theta f(x;\theta)\vert_{\theta_{MAP}}\) the output covariance matrix \( \mathcal{J} P^{-1} \mathcal{J}^T \).

    def functional_variance(self, Js: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    self._check_jacobians(Js)
    return torch.einsum("...cp,p,...kp->...ck", Js, self.posterior_variance, Js)

    functional_covariance #

    functional_covariance(Js: Tensor) -> Tensor

    Compute functional covariance for the 'glm' predictive: f_cov = Js @ P.inv() @ Js.T, which is a batchoutput x batchoutput predictive covariance matrix.

    This emulates the GP posterior covariance N([f(x1), ...,f(xm)], Cov[f(x1), ..., f(xm)]). Useful for joint predictions, such as in batched Bayesian optimization.

    Parameters:

    • Js (Tensor) –

      Jacobians of model output wrt parameters ([batch_dims], outputs, parameters)

    Returns:

      output covariance (batch*outputs, batch*outputs)

    def functional_covariance(self, Js: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    self._check_jacobians(Js)
    # (prod(batch_dims) * out_dim, n_params)
    Js = Js.reshape(-1, Js.shape[-1])
    # (prod(batch_dims) * out_dim, prod(batch_dims) * out_dim)
    cov = torch.einsum("np,p,mp->nm", Js, self.posterior_variance, Js)
    return cov

    def _check_subnetwork_indices(
    self, subnetwork_indices: torch.LongTensor | None
) -> None:
    """Check that subnetwork indices are valid indices of the vectorized model parameters
    (i.e. `torch.nn.utils.parameters_to_vector(model.parameters())`).
    """
    if subnetwork_indices is None:
        raise ValueError("Subnetwork indices cannot be None.")
    elif not (
        isinstance(subnetwork_indices, torch.LongTensor)
        and subnetwork_indices.numel() > 0
        and len(subnetwork_indices.shape) == 1
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            "Subnetwork indices must be non-empty 1-dimensional torch.LongTensor."
        )
    elif not (
        len(subnetwork_indices[subnetwork_indices < 0]) == 0
        and len(subnetwork_indices[subnetwork_indices >= self.n_params]) == 0
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Subnetwork indices must lie between 0 and n_params={self.n_params}."
        )
    elif not (len(subnetwork_indices.unique()) == len(subnetwork_indices)):
        raise ValueError("Subnetwork indices must not contain duplicate entries.")

    def sample(
    self, n_samples: int = 100, generator: torch.Generator | None = None
) -> torch.Tensor:
    # sample only subnetwork parameters and set all other parameters to their MAP estimates
    samples = torch.randn(
        n_samples, self.n_params_subnet, device=self._device, generator=generator
    )
    samples = samples * self.posterior_scale.reshape(1, self.n_params_subnet)
    subnet_samples = self.mean_subnet.reshape(1, self.n_params_subnet) + samples
    return self.assemble_full_samples(subnet_samples)

    def __init__(
    self,
    model: nn.Module,
    likelihood: Likelihood | str | nn.Module,
    subnetwork_indices: torch.LongTensor,
    sigma_noise: float | torch.Tensor = 1.0,
    prior_precision: float | torch.Tensor = 1.0,
    prior_mean: float | torch.Tensor = 0.0,
    temperature: float = 1.0,
    backend: Type[CurvatureInterface] | None = None,
    backend_kwargs: dict | None = None,
    asdl_fisher_kwargs: dict | None = None,
    *,
    dict_key_x: str = "input_ids",
    dict_key_y: str = "labels",
) -> None:
    if asdl_fisher_kwargs is not None:
        raise ValueError("Subnetwork Laplace does not support asdl_fisher_kwargs.")

    self.H = None
    super().__init__(
        model,
        likelihood,
        sigma_noise=sigma_noise,
        prior_precision=prior_precision,
        prior_mean=prior_mean,
        temperature=temperature,
        dict_key_x=dict_key_x,
        dict_key_y=dict_key_y,
        backend=backend,
        backend_kwargs=backend_kwargs,
    )

    if backend is not None and not issubclass(backend, (GGNInterface, EFInterface)):
        raise ValueError("SubnetLaplace can only be used with GGN and EF.")

    # check validity of subnetwork indices and pass them to backend
    self._check_subnetwork_indices(subnetwork_indices)
    self._subnetwork_indices = subnetwork_indices
    self.backend.subnetwork_indices = subnetwork_indices
    self.n_params_subnet = len(subnetwork_indices)
    self._init_H()

    def _stage_likelihood(self, fitting: bool) -> Likelihood:
    """The fit likelihood while fitting, else the predictive likelihood. The two
    differ only for reward modeling.
    """
    if fitting:
        return self.likelihood.fit_likelihood

    return self.likelihood.predictive_likelihood

    def __setstate__(self, state: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Restore a pickled instance.

    Pickles made before `_subnetwork_indices` existed keep the indices only on the
    cached backend. They are copied over, so that rebuilding the backend (e.g.
    after a likelihood change) keeps the subnetwork.

    Parameters
    ----------
    state : dict[str, Any]
        the pickled `__dict__`.
    """
    super().__setstate__(state)

    if "_subnetwork_indices" not in vars(self) and self._backend is not None:
        self._subnetwork_indices = self._backend.subnetwork_indices

    def log_marginal_likelihood(
    self,
    prior_precision: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    sigma_noise: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Compute the Laplace approximation to the log marginal likelihood subject
    to specific Hessian approximations that subclasses implement.
    Requires that the Laplace approximation has been fit before.
    The resulting torch.Tensor is differentiable in `prior_precision` and
    `sigma_noise` if these have gradients enabled.
    By passing `prior_precision` or `sigma_noise`, the current value is
    overwritten. This is useful for iterating on the log marginal likelihood.

    Parameters
    ----------
    prior_precision : torch.Tensor, optional
        prior precision if should be changed from current `prior_precision` value
    sigma_noise : torch.Tensor, optional
        observation noise standard deviation if should be changed

    Returns
    -------
    log_marglik : torch.Tensor
    """
    # update prior precision (useful when iterating on marglik)
    if prior_precision is not None:
        self.prior_precision = prior_precision

    # update sigma_noise (useful when iterating on marglik)
    if sigma_noise is not None:
        if not self.likelihood.is_gaussian:
            raise ValueError("Can only change sigma_noise for regression.")

        self.sigma_noise = sigma_noise

    return self.log_likelihood - 0.5 * (self.log_det_ratio + self.scatter)

    __call__ #

    __call__(
    x: Tensor | MutableMapping[str, Tensor | Any],
    pred_type: PredType | str = PredType.GLM,
    joint: bool = False,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str = LinkApprox.PROBIT,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    diagonal_output: bool = False,
    generator: Generator | None = None,
    fitting: bool = False,
    **model_kwargs: dict[str, Any]
) -> Tensor | tuple[Tensor, Tensor]

    Compute the posterior predictive on input data x.

    Parameters:

    • x (Tensor or MutableMapping) –

      (batch_size, input_shape) if tensor. If MutableMapping, must contain the said tensor.

    • pred_type (('glm', 'nn'), default: 'glm' ) –

      type of posterior predictive, linearized GLM predictive or neural network sampling predictive. The GLM predictive is consistent with the curvature approximations used here. It also works when Laplace is done on a subset of the parameters, either with subnetwork Laplace or by disabling the gradients of the other parameters.

    • link_approx (('mc', 'probit', 'bridge', 'bridge_norm'), default: 'mc' ) –

      how to approximate the classification link function for the 'glm'. For pred_type='nn', only 'mc' is possible. Likelihoods other than classification and reward modeling always use Monte Carlo.

    • joint (bool, default: False ) –

      Whether to output a joint predictive distribution in regression with pred_type='glm'. If set to True, the predictive distribution has the same form as GP posterior, i.e. N([f(x1), ...,f(xm)], Cov[f(x1), ..., f(xm)]). If False, then only outputs the marginal predictive distribution. Only available for regression and GLM predictive.

    • n_samples (int, default: 100 ) –

      number of samples for link_approx='mc', for pred_type='nn', and for the Monte Carlo predictive of other likelihoods.

    • diagonal_output (bool, default: False ) –

      whether to use a diagonalized posterior predictive on the outputs. Only works for pred_type='glm' when joint=False in regression. With last-layer Laplace and a diagonal Hessian, setting it to True skips the Jacobians, which is much faster for many outputs.

    • generator (Generator, default: None ) –

      random number generator to control the samples (if sampling used).

    • fitting (bool, default: False ) –

      whether or not this predictive call is done during fitting. Only useful for reward modeling: the likelihood is set to "regression" when False and "classification" when True.

    Returns:

    • predictive ( Tensor or tuple[Tensor] ) –

      For likelihood='classification', a torch.Tensor is returned with a distribution over classes (similar to a Softmax), with the same shape as the logits, e.g. (batch, classes) or (batch, seq_len, classes). For likelihood='regression', a tuple of torch.Tensor is returned with the mean and the predictive variance. For likelihood='regression' and joint=True, a tuple of torch.Tensor is returned with the mean and the predictive covariance. For likelihood='heteroscedastic_gaussian', a tuple (f_mean, f_alea, f_epis) is returned: the mean and the variance that the network predicts, and the epistemic covariance of the mean, or its variance with pred_type='nn' or diagonal_output=True. For any other likelihood, a torch.Tensor with the shape of the outputs is returned. It averages the likelihood's inverse_link over n_samples draws of the outputs from the GLM predictive or from the weight posterior.

    Warns:

    • RuntimeWarning –

      For "bridge" and "bridge_norm" when gradient tracking is enabled and a covariance requiring gradients has subnormal, nonzero magnitude for an input row. Magnitude is the largest absolute covariance entry, compared with the smallest positive normal value of the covariance dtype.

    Notes

    The "bridge" and "bridge_norm" links use float64 intermediate calculations and return probabilities in the predictive mean's dtype. Mean corrections and normalization use scaled logit differences to avoid overflow. If corrected variances or the optional normalization scale are nonpositive, or the Bridge probabilities are nonfinite, prediction uses the probit approximation on centered moments before variance normalization. Corrected variances are clamped at zero for this fallback.

    For subnormal covariance magnitudes, covariance-entry derivatives can exceed their dtype's range. Covariance or upstream parameter gradients may therefore contain inf or NaN even when probabilities remain finite. Covariance backpropagation is not reliable in this regime. A RuntimeWarning is emitted when covariance gradients are tracked.

    def __call__(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    pred_type: PredType | str = PredType.GLM,
    joint: bool = False,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str = LinkApprox.PROBIT,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    diagonal_output: bool = False,
    generator: torch.Generator | None = None,
    fitting: bool = False,
    **model_kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute the posterior predictive on input data `x`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        `(batch_size, input_shape)` if tensor. If MutableMapping, must contain
        the said tensor.

    pred_type : {'glm', 'nn'}, default='glm'
        type of posterior predictive, linearized GLM predictive or neural
        network sampling predictive. The GLM predictive is consistent with
        the curvature approximations used here. It also works when Laplace
        is done on a subset of the parameters, either with subnetwork
        Laplace or by disabling the gradients of the other parameters.

    link_approx : {'mc', 'probit', 'bridge', 'bridge_norm'}
        how to approximate the classification link function for the `'glm'`.
        For `pred_type='nn'`, only 'mc' is possible. Likelihoods other than
        classification and reward modeling always use Monte Carlo.

    joint : bool
        Whether to output a joint predictive distribution in regression with
        `pred_type='glm'`. If set to `True`, the predictive distribution
        has the same form as GP posterior, i.e. N([f(x1), ...,f(xm)], Cov[f(x1), ..., f(xm)]).
        If `False`, then only outputs the marginal predictive distribution.
        Only available for regression and GLM predictive.

    n_samples : int
        number of samples for `link_approx='mc'`, for `pred_type='nn'`, and
        for the Monte Carlo predictive of other likelihoods.

    diagonal_output : bool
        whether to use a diagonalized posterior predictive on the outputs.
        Only works for `pred_type='glm'` when `joint=False` in regression.
        With last-layer Laplace and a diagonal Hessian, setting it to `True`
        skips the Jacobians, which is much faster for many outputs.

    generator : torch.Generator, optional
        random number generator to control the samples (if sampling used).

    fitting : bool, default=False
        whether or not this predictive call is done during fitting. Only useful for
        reward modeling: the likelihood is set to `"regression"` when `False` and
        `"classification"` when `True`.

    Returns
    -------
    predictive: torch.Tensor or tuple[torch.Tensor]
        For `likelihood='classification'`, a torch.Tensor is returned with
        a distribution over classes (similar to a Softmax), with the same shape
        as the logits, e.g. `(batch, classes)` or `(batch, seq_len, classes)`.
        For `likelihood='regression'`, a tuple of torch.Tensor is returned
        with the mean and the predictive variance.
        For `likelihood='regression'` and `joint=True`, a tuple of torch.Tensor
        is returned with the mean and the predictive covariance.
        For `likelihood='heteroscedastic_gaussian'`, a tuple
        `(f_mean, f_alea, f_epis)` is returned: the mean and the variance that
        the network predicts, and the epistemic covariance of the mean, or its
        variance with `pred_type='nn'` or `diagonal_output=True`.
        For any other likelihood, a torch.Tensor with the shape of the outputs
        is returned. It averages the likelihood's `inverse_link` over
        `n_samples` draws of the outputs from the GLM predictive or from the
        weight posterior.

    Warns
    -----
    RuntimeWarning
        For ``"bridge"`` and ``"bridge_norm"`` when gradient tracking is
        enabled and a covariance requiring gradients has subnormal,
        nonzero magnitude for an input row. Magnitude is the largest
        absolute covariance entry, compared with the smallest positive
        normal value of the covariance dtype.

    Notes
    -----
    The ``"bridge"`` and ``"bridge_norm"`` links use float64 intermediate
    calculations and return probabilities in the predictive mean's dtype.
    Mean corrections and normalization use scaled logit differences to
    avoid overflow.
    If corrected variances or the optional normalization scale are
    nonpositive, or the Bridge probabilities are nonfinite, prediction uses
    the probit approximation on centered moments before variance
    normalization. Corrected variances are clamped at zero for this fallback.

    For subnormal covariance magnitudes, covariance-entry derivatives can
    exceed their dtype's range. Covariance or upstream parameter gradients
    may therefore contain inf or NaN even when probabilities remain finite.
    Covariance backpropagation is not reliable in this regime. A
    RuntimeWarning is emitted when covariance gradients are tracked.
    """
    if pred_type not in [pred for pred in PredType]:
        raise ValueError("Only glm and nn supported as prediction types.")

    if link_approx not in [la for la in LinkApprox]:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported link approximation {link_approx}.")

    if pred_type == PredType.NN and link_approx != LinkApprox.MC:
        raise ValueError(
            "Only mc link approximation is supported for nn prediction type."
        )

    if generator is not None:
        if (
            not isinstance(generator, torch.Generator)
            or generator.device != self._device
        ):
            raise ValueError("Invalid random generator (check type and device).")

    if _is_heteroscedastic(self.likelihood):
        # The predictive is a Gaussian over the mean, also while fitting
        with joined_outputs(self.model):
            f_mean, f_epis = self._predictive(
                x,
                self.likelihood.predictive_likelihood,
                pred_type,
                joint,
                link_approx,
                n_samples,
                diagonal_output,
                generator,
                **model_kwargs,
            )

        f_alea = self._aleatoric_variance(x, joint, **model_kwargs)

        return f_mean, f_alea, f_epis

    return self._predictive(
        x,
        self._stage_likelihood(fitting),
        pred_type,
        joint,
        link_approx,
        n_samples,
        diagonal_output,
        generator,
        **model_kwargs,
    )

    optimize_prior_precision #

    optimize_prior_precision(
    pred_type: PredType | str = PredType.GLM,
    method: TuningMethod | str = TuningMethod.MARGLIK,
    n_steps: int = 100,
    lr: float = 0.1,
    init_prior_prec: float | Tensor = 1.0,
    prior_structure: (
        PriorStructure | str
    ) = PriorStructure.SCALAR,
    val_loader: DataLoader | None = None,
    loss: (
        Metric | Callable[[Tensor], Tensor | float] | None
    ) = None,
    log_prior_prec_min: float = -4,
    log_prior_prec_max: float = 4,
    grid_size: int = 100,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str = LinkApprox.PROBIT,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    verbose: bool = False,
    progress_bar: bool = False,
    log_prior_prec_base: float = 10.0,
) -> None

    Optimize the prior precision post-hoc using the method specified by the user.

    Parameters:

    • pred_type (PredType or str in {'glm', 'nn'}) –

      type of posterior predictive, linearized GLM predictive or neural network sampling predictiv. The GLM predictive is consistent with the curvature approximations used here.

    • method (TuningMethod or str in {'marglik', 'gridsearch'}, default: PredType.MARGLIK ) –

      specifies how the prior precision should be optimized.

    • n_steps (int, default: 100 ) –

      the number of gradient descent steps to take.

    • lr (float, default: 1e-1 ) –

      the learning rate to use for gradient descent.

    • init_prior_prec (float or tensor, default: 1.0 ) –

      initial prior precision before the first optimization step.

    • prior_structure (PriorStructure or str in {'scalar', 'layerwise', 'diag'}, default: PriorStructure.SCALAR ) –

      if init_prior_prec is scalar, the prior precision is optimized with this structure. otherwise, the structure of init_prior_prec is maintained.

    • val_loader (DataLoader, default: None ) –

      DataLoader for the validation set; each iterate is a training batch (X, y).

    • loss (callable or Metric, default: None ) –

      loss function to use for CV. If callable, the loss is computed offline (memory intensive). If torchmetrics.Metric, running loss is computed (efficient). The default depends on the likelihood: RunningNLLMetric() for classification and reward modeling, with the ignore_index of a CategoricalLikelihood, RunningBernoulliNLLMetric() for the Bernoulli likelihood, RunningGaussianNLLMetric() for the heteroscedastic Gaussian likelihood, and for regression RunningGaussianNLLMetric with the noise variance of the likelihood. Other likelihoods have no default, so loss is required for them.

    • log_prior_prec_min (float, default: -4 ) –

      exponent of the lower bound of the gridsearch interval.

    • log_prior_prec_max (float, default: 4 ) –

      exponent of the upper bound of the gridsearch interval.

    • grid_size (int, default: 100 ) –

      number of values to consider inside the gridsearch interval.

    • link_approx (LinkApprox or str in {'mc', 'probit', 'bridge'}, default: LinkApprox.PROBIT ) –

      how to approximate the classification link function for the 'glm'. For pred_type='nn', only 'mc' is possible.

    • n_samples (int, default: 100 ) –

      number of samples for link_approx='mc'.

    • verbose (bool, default: False ) –

      if true, the optimized prior precision will be printed (can be a large tensor if the prior has a diagonal covariance).

    • progress_bar (bool, default: False ) –

      whether to show a progress bar; updated at every batch-Hessian computation. Useful for very large model and large amount of data, esp. when subset_of_weights='all'.

    • log_prior_prec_base (float, default: 10.0 ) –

      base of the logarithmic gridsearch interval. The bounds are log_prior_prec_base raised to log_prior_prec_min and log_prior_prec_max.

    def optimize_prior_precision(
    self,
    pred_type: PredType | str = PredType.GLM,
    method: TuningMethod | str = TuningMethod.MARGLIK,
    n_steps: int = 100,
    lr: float = 1e-1,
    init_prior_prec: float | torch.Tensor = 1.0,
    prior_structure: PriorStructure | str = PriorStructure.SCALAR,
    val_loader: DataLoader | None = None,
    loss: torchmetrics.Metric
    | Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor | float]
    | None = None,
    log_prior_prec_min: float = -4,
    log_prior_prec_max: float = 4,
    grid_size: int = 100,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str = LinkApprox.PROBIT,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    verbose: bool = False,
    progress_bar: bool = False,
    log_prior_prec_base: float = 10.0,
) -> None:
    assert pred_type in PredType.__members__.values()

    super().optimize_prior_precision(
        pred_type,
        method,
        n_steps,
        lr,
        init_prior_prec,
        prior_structure,
        val_loader,
        loss,
        log_prior_prec_min,
        log_prior_prec_max,
        grid_size,
        link_approx,
        n_samples,
        verbose,
        progress_bar,
        log_prior_prec_base=log_prior_prec_base,
    )

    def _glm_predictive_marginals(
    self, x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Mean and variance of each output of the GLM predictive, without the
    covariances between outputs. Override it when the variances are cheaper to
    get than the full output covariance.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        inputs, as in `__call__`.

    Returns
    -------
    f_mu : torch.Tensor
        predictive mean `(batch, outputs)`
    f_var : torch.Tensor
        predictive variances `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    f_mu, f_var = self._glm_predictive_distribution(x)

    return f_mu, torch.diagonal(f_var, dim1=-2, dim2=-1)

    _glm_forward_call(
    x: Tensor | MutableMapping,
    likelihood: Likelihood | str,
    joint: bool = False,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str = LinkApprox.PROBIT,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    diagonal_output: bool = False,
    generator: Generator | None = None,

    Compute the posterior predictive on input data x for "glm" pred type.

    Parameters:

    • x (Tensor or MutableMapping) –

      (batch_size, input_shape) if tensor. If MutableMapping, must contain the said tensor.

    • likelihood (Likelihood or str) –

      likelihood of the predictive. A Gaussian one returns the predictive moments. Classification and reward modeling return class probabilities from link_approx. Any other likelihood returns the Monte Carlo estimate of \(\mathbb{E}[g(f)]\) under the GLM predictive \(f \sim \mathcal{N}(f_\mu, \Sigma_f)\), where \(g\) is its inverse_link, from n_samples draws.

    • link_approx (('mc', 'probit', 'bridge', 'bridge_norm'), default: 'mc' ) –

      how to approximate the classification link function for the 'glm'. For pred_type='nn', only 'mc' is possible. Likelihoods other than classification, reward modeling and Bernoulli always use Monte Carlo.

    • joint (bool, default: False ) –

      Whether to output a joint predictive distribution in regression with pred_type='glm'. If set to True, the predictive distribution has the same form as GP posterior, i.e. N([f(x1), ...,f(xm)], Cov[f(x1), ..., f(xm)]). If False, then only outputs the marginal predictive distribution. Only available for regression and GLM predictive.

    • n_samples (int, default: 100 ) –

      number of samples for link_approx='mc' and for the Monte Carlo predictive of other likelihoods.

    • diagonal_output (bool, default: False ) –

      whether to use a diagonalized posterior predictive on the outputs. Only works for pred_type='glm' and link_approx='mc', or for the Monte Carlo predictive of other likelihoods.

    • generator (Generator, default: None ) –

      random number generator for the Monte Carlo samples.

    Returns:

    • predictive ( Tensor or tuple[Tensor] ) –

      For likelihood='classification', a torch.Tensor is returned with a distribution over classes (similar to a Softmax), with the same shape as the logits, e.g. (batch, classes) or (batch, seq_len, classes). For likelihood='regression', a tuple of torch.Tensor is returned with the mean and the predictive variance. For likelihood='regression' and joint=True, a tuple of torch.Tensor is returned with the mean and the predictive covariance. For any other likelihood, a torch.Tensor is returned with the predictive mean of the targets, with the shape of the outputs, e.g. (batch, outputs).

    Warns:

    • RuntimeWarning –

      For "bridge" and "bridge_norm" when gradient tracking is enabled and a covariance requiring gradients has subnormal, nonzero magnitude for an input row. Magnitude is the largest absolute covariance entry, compared with the smallest positive normal value of the covariance dtype.

    Notes

    The "bridge" and "bridge_norm" links use float64 intermediate calculations and return probabilities in the predictive mean's dtype. Mean corrections and normalization use scaled logit differences to avoid overflow. If corrected variances or the optional normalization scale are nonpositive, or the Bridge probabilities are nonfinite, prediction uses the probit approximation on centered moments before variance normalization. Corrected variances are clamped at zero for this fallback.

    For subnormal covariance magnitudes, covariance-entry derivatives can exceed their dtype's range. Covariance or upstream parameter gradients may therefore contain inf or NaN even when probabilities remain finite. Covariance backpropagation is not reliable in this regime. A RuntimeWarning is emitted when covariance gradients are tracked.

    def _glm_forward_call(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping,
    likelihood: Likelihood | str,
    joint: bool = False,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str = LinkApprox.PROBIT,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    diagonal_output: bool = False,
    generator: torch.Generator | None = None,
) -> torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute the posterior predictive on input data `x` for "glm" pred type.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        `(batch_size, input_shape)` if tensor. If MutableMapping, must contain
        the said tensor.

    likelihood : Likelihood or str
        likelihood of the predictive. A Gaussian one returns the predictive
        moments. Classification and reward modeling return class probabilities
        from `link_approx`. Any other likelihood returns the Monte Carlo
        estimate of \\(\\mathbb{E}[g(f)]\\) under the GLM predictive
        \\(f \\sim \\mathcal{N}(f_\\mu, \\Sigma_f)\\), where \\(g\\) is its
        `inverse_link`, from `n_samples` draws.

    link_approx : {'mc', 'probit', 'bridge', 'bridge_norm'}
        how to approximate the classification link function for the `'glm'`.
        For `pred_type='nn'`, only 'mc' is possible. Likelihoods other than
        classification, reward modeling and Bernoulli always use Monte Carlo.

    joint : bool
        Whether to output a joint predictive distribution in regression with
        `pred_type='glm'`. If set to `True`, the predictive distribution
        has the same form as GP posterior, i.e. N([f(x1), ...,f(xm)], Cov[f(x1), ..., f(xm)]).
        If `False`, then only outputs the marginal predictive distribution.
        Only available for regression and GLM predictive.

    n_samples : int
        number of samples for `link_approx='mc'` and for the Monte Carlo
        predictive of other likelihoods.

    diagonal_output : bool
        whether to use a diagonalized posterior predictive on the outputs.
        Only works for `pred_type='glm'` and `link_approx='mc'`, or for the
        Monte Carlo predictive of other likelihoods.

    generator : torch.Generator, optional
        random number generator for the Monte Carlo samples.

    Returns
    -------
    predictive: torch.Tensor or tuple[torch.Tensor]
        For `likelihood='classification'`, a torch.Tensor is returned with
        a distribution over classes (similar to a Softmax), with the same shape
        as the logits, e.g. `(batch, classes)` or `(batch, seq_len, classes)`.
        For `likelihood='regression'`, a tuple of torch.Tensor is returned
        with the mean and the predictive variance.
        For `likelihood='regression'` and `joint=True`, a tuple of torch.Tensor
        is returned with the mean and the predictive covariance.
        For any other likelihood, a torch.Tensor is returned with the predictive
        mean of the targets, with the shape of the outputs, e.g.
        `(batch, outputs)`.

    Warns
    -----
    RuntimeWarning
        For ``"bridge"`` and ``"bridge_norm"`` when gradient tracking is
        enabled and a covariance requiring gradients has subnormal,
        nonzero magnitude for an input row. Magnitude is the largest
        absolute covariance entry, compared with the smallest positive
        normal value of the covariance dtype.

    Notes
    -----
    The ``"bridge"`` and ``"bridge_norm"`` links use float64 intermediate
    calculations and return probabilities in the predictive mean's dtype.
    Mean corrections and normalization use scaled logit differences to
    avoid overflow.
    If corrected variances or the optional normalization scale are
    nonpositive, or the Bridge probabilities are nonfinite, prediction uses
    the probit approximation on centered moments before variance
    normalization. Corrected variances are clamped at zero for this fallback.

    For subnormal covariance magnitudes, covariance-entry derivatives can
    exceed their dtype's range. Covariance or upstream parameter gradients
    may therefore contain inf or NaN even when probabilities remain finite.
    Covariance backpropagation is not reliable in this regime. A
    RuntimeWarning is emitted when covariance gradients are tracked.
    """
    likelihood = get_likelihood(likelihood)
    is_gaussian = likelihood.is_gaussian

    if is_gaussian and diagonal_output and not joint:
        return self._glm_predictive_marginals(x)

    f_mu, f_var = self._glm_predictive_distribution(x, joint=joint and is_gaussian)

    if is_gaussian:
        return f_mu, f_var

    if likelihood.name == Likelihood.BERNOULLI.name:
        # Every output has its own sigmoid, so the probit approximation needs only
        # the marginal variances. MC falls through to the generic path below.
        if link_approx == LinkApprox.PROBIT:
            kappa = 1 / torch.sqrt(
                1.0 + np.pi / 8 * torch.diagonal(f_var, dim1=-2, dim2=-1)
            )
            return likelihood.inverse_link(kappa * f_mu)

        if link_approx != LinkApprox.MC:
            raise ValueError(
                "The Laplace bridge is for the softmax link only. Use 'probit' or "
                "'mc' with the Bernoulli likelihood."
            )

    if likelihood.name not in _CATEGORICAL_NAMES:
        # No closed form to approximate, so integrate the inverse link by MC
        f_samples = self._glm_functional_samples(
            f_mu, f_var, n_samples, diagonal_output, generator
        )
        return likelihood.inverse_link(f_samples).mean(dim=0)

    # Every leading dim of the logits but the last is a batch dim, e.g. `(B, L, C)`
    # for sequences. The link approximations work on `(N, C)`, so flatten them.
    batch_shape = f_mu.shape[:-1]
    f_mu = f_mu.reshape(-1, f_mu.shape[-1])
    f_var = f_var.reshape(-1, *f_var.shape[-2:])

    probs = self._glm_classification_link(
        f_mu, f_var, likelihood, link_approx, n_samples, diagonal_output, generator
    )
    return probs.reshape(*batch_shape, probs.shape[-1])

    def _glm_classification_link(
    self,
    f_mu: torch.Tensor,
    f_var: torch.Tensor,
    likelihood: Likelihood,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str,
    n_samples: int,
    diagonal_output: bool,
    generator: torch.Generator | None = None,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Approximate the predictive class probabilities from the GLM predictive
    `f_mu` `(batch, classes)` and `f_var` `(batch, classes, classes)`. `likelihood`
    is the staged likelihood, categorical while fitting a reward model. See
    `_glm_forward_call` for the other arguments.
    """
    if link_approx == LinkApprox.MC:
        f_samples = self._glm_functional_samples(
            f_mu, f_var, n_samples, diagonal_output, generator
        )
        return likelihood.inverse_link(f_samples).mean(dim=0)
    elif link_approx == LinkApprox.PROBIT:
        kappa = 1 / torch.sqrt(1.0 + np.pi / 8 * f_var.diagonal(dim1=1, dim2=2))
        return torch.softmax(kappa * f_mu, dim=-1)
    elif "bridge" in link_approx:
        _, K = f_mu.shape
        if K == 1:
            return torch.ones_like(f_mu)

        # Float32 reductions can overflow even when every input is finite.
        # Keep the link calculation in double precision, then restore the
        # predictive dtype at the return boundary.
        output_dtype, covariance_dtype = f_mu.dtype, f_var.dtype
        work_dtype = torch.promote_types(output_dtype, covariance_dtype)
        if work_dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32):
            work_dtype = torch.float64
        f_mu, f_var = f_mu.to(work_dtype), f_var.to(work_dtype)

        # Normalize covariance before reductions: even float64 sums can
        # overflow when each covariance entry is finite. The scale
        # cancels in the ratio, so detach it to avoid unstable gradients
        # through the normalization itself.
        covariance_scale = f_var.detach().abs().amax(dim=(1, 2), keepdim=True)
        if (
            torch.is_grad_enabled()
            and f_var.requires_grad
            and (
                (covariance_scale > 0)
                & (covariance_scale < torch.finfo(covariance_dtype).tiny)
            ).any()
        ):
            warnings.warn(
                "Bridge covariance gradients may overflow for subnormal covariance, "
                "even when probabilities are finite. Covariance and upstream "
                "parameter gradients may contain inf or NaN; covariance "
                "backpropagation is not reliable at this scale.",
                RuntimeWarning,
                stacklevel=3,
            )
        safe_covariance_scale = torch.where(
            covariance_scale > 0, covariance_scale, 1
        )
        scaled_covariance = f_var / safe_covariance_scale
        row_sums = scaled_covariance.sum(dim=-1)
        sum_variance = row_sums.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True).unsqueeze(-1)
        centered = sum_variance.abs() <= (
            torch.finfo(covariance_dtype).eps
            * scaled_covariance.abs().sum(dim=(1, 2), keepdim=True)
        )
        safe_variance = torch.where(centered, 1, sum_variance)
        ratio = torch.where(
            centered.squeeze(-1), 0, row_sums / safe_variance.squeeze(-1)
        )

        # Keep the mean correction scaled: even subtracting two finite
        # float64 means can overflow. Only restore the scale after removing
        # a common shift, since Bridge depends on logit differences.
        mean_magnitude = f_mu.detach().abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        _, mean_exponent = torch.frexp(mean_magnitude)
        # Bound both scales to leave headroom for normalization gradients.
        # A power of two preserves representable logit differences; exp2
        # with an explicit dtype is independent of the global default.
        logit_limit = sqrt(sqrt(torch.finfo(work_dtype).max))
        max_mean_exponent = frexp(logit_limit)[1] - 1
        mean_scale = torch.exp2(
            (mean_exponent - 1).clamp(0, max_mean_exponent).to(work_dtype)
        )
        scaled_mean = f_mu / mean_scale
        mean_logit = (scaled_mean / K).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        scaled_mean = scaled_mean - torch.where(
            centered.squeeze(-1),
            mean_logit,
            (K * ratio) * mean_logit,
        )
        f_mu = scaled_mean - scaled_mean.amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        centered_covariance = scaled_covariance - ratio.unsqueeze(
            -1
        ) * row_sums.unsqueeze(-2)
        scaled_var_diag = centered_covariance.diagonal(dim1=-2, dim2=-1)
        centered_var_diag = scaled_var_diag * safe_covariance_scale.squeeze(-1)
        valid_variance = (centered_var_diag > 0).all(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        normalization = torch.ones_like(mean_scale)

        if link_approx == LinkApprox.BRIDGE_NORM:
            variance_scale = (centered_var_diag / K).sum(
                dim=-1, keepdim=True
            ) / sqrt(K / 2)
            valid_variance = valid_variance & (variance_scale > 0)
            normalization = torch.where(valid_variance, variance_scale, 1).sqrt()

        # Bound normalized differences before division, so saturated
        # branches cannot overflow in either forward or backward passes.
        # The detached bound is far beyond exponential underflow; large
        # variances still bring extreme gaps back into a meaningful range.
        minimum_logit = -(logit_limit / mean_scale) * normalization.detach()
        f_mu = (f_mu.clamp_min(minimum_logit) / normalization) * mean_scale

        # Normalize the Bridge's Dirichlet parameters in log space.
        # The log-sum-exp term is common to every class and cancels in
        # the final softmax. Remove it before combining the numerator
        # terms, avoiding overflow when finite logit gaps are enormous.
        log_sum_negative = torch.logsumexp(-f_mu, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        log_base = log(1 - 2 / K) if K > 2 else -float("inf")
        log_numerator = torch.logaddexp(
            torch.full_like(f_mu, log_base) - log_sum_negative,
            f_mu - 2 * log(K),
        )
        # Remove the common offset before subtracting log-variance,
        # preserving variance-dependent weights for tied large logits.
        log_numerator = log_numerator - log_numerator.amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        if K == 2:
            # Binary corrected variances are equal for symmetric covariance.
            # Cancel their common term before differentiation to avoid
            # overflowing gradients for subnormal covariance.
            log_alpha = log_numerator
        else:
            # Common covariance and optional variance scales cancel in alpha
            # normalization. Logging the scaled diagonal avoids reciprocals
            # of subnormal variances in backpropagation.
            log_alpha = (
                log_numerator
                - scaled_var_diag.clamp_min(torch.finfo(work_dtype).tiny).log()
            )
        probabilities = torch.softmax(log_alpha, dim=-1)

        # A common shift of every logit has no effect on softmax. The
        # fallback therefore uses the centered moments before Bridge's
        # optional variance normalization.
        fallback_logits = scaled_mean / torch.sqrt(
            1 + np.pi / 8 * centered_var_diag.clamp_min(0)
        )
        fallback_logits = fallback_logits - fallback_logits.amax(
            dim=-1, keepdim=True
        )
        fallback_logits = (
            fallback_logits.clamp_min(-logit_limit / mean_scale) * mean_scale
        )
        fallback = torch.softmax(fallback_logits, dim=-1)
        valid_variance = valid_variance & torch.isfinite(probabilities).all(
            dim=-1, keepdim=True
        )
        return torch.where(valid_variance, probabilities, fallback).to(output_dtype)
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            "Prediction path invalid. Check the likelihood, pred_type, link_approx combination!"
        )

    functional_samples(
    x: Tensor | MutableMapping[str, Tensor | Any],

    Sample from the function-space posterior on input data x. Can be used, for example, to compute an arbitrary expectation, or with joint=True for Thompson sampling.

    Parameters:

    • x (Tensor or MutableMapping) –

      input data (batch_size, input_shape)

    • pred_type (('glm', 'nn'), default: 'glm' ) –

      type of posterior predictive, linearized GLM predictive or neural network sampling predictive. The GLM predictive is consistent with the curvature approximations used here.

    • n_samples (int, default: 100 ) –

      number of samples

    • diagonal_output (bool, default: False ) –

      whether to use a diagonalized glm posterior predictive on the outputs. Only applies when pred_type='glm'.

    • generator (Generator, default: None ) –

      random number generator to control the samples (if sampling used)

    • joint (bool, default: False ) –

      whether to sample all inputs in x jointly. With joint=False, each input's marginal is correct but the samples ignore the correlation between inputs. Use joint=True for Thompson sampling or batch acquisition functions such as qEI. The joint covariance has (batch_size * outputs)**2 entries, so memory grows quadratically with the batch. Extra batch dimensions are flattened into batch_size. Ignored when pred_type='nn', since one weight sample already gives one function over all inputs.

    Returns:

    • samples ( Tensor ) –

      samples (n_samples, batch_size, output_shape)
